name: deep_nesting
description: Five levels of nested ifs; guard clauses flatten it. One quirk must survive: insurance only applies to express.

files.tests/test_rates.py:
import pytest

from shipping.rates import shipping_cost


def test_standard_and_express():
    assert shipping_cost(2, "NL") == 5.0
    assert shipping_cost(2, "NL", express=True) == 7.5


def test_errors():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive"):
        shipping_cost(0, "NL")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unknown destination: FR"):
        shipping_cost(1, "FR")

import pytest

from shipping.rates import shipping_cost


def test_insurance_only_applies_to_express():
    assert shipping_cost(10, "DE", insured=True) == 14.0
    assert shipping_cost(10, "DE", express=True, insured=True) == 31.0


def test_weight_limit_and_error_order():
    assert shipping_cost(30, "US") == 57.0
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="too heavy"):
        shipping_cost(31, "US")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive"):  # checked before the destination
        shipping_cost(-1, "FR")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unknown destination"):  # before the weight limit
        shipping_cost(99, "FR")
